questions.question: The boiling point of water is _____
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**100º C**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The boiling point of water is 100º C at standard atmospheric pressure (1 atmosphere).
 
• At this temperature, water transitions from a liquid state to a gaseous state (steam).
 
• The boiling point can vary depending on the atmospheric pressure; it is lower at higher altitudes where the atmospheric pressure is less.
 
• 100º C corresponds to 373.15 K in Kelvin scale.
 
• Boiling point is a physical property of a substance, and it is used to characterize and identify substances.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Freezing Point of Water**

 
 
• The freezing point of water is 0º C (32º F) at standard atmospheric pressure.
 
• At this temperature, water transitions from a liquid state to a solid state (ice).
 
 
 
• **Melting Point**
 
 
• The melting point of ice is the same as the freezing point of water, which is 0º C (32º F).
 
• At this temperature, ice transitions from a solid state to a liquid state (water).
 
 
 
• **Sublimation**
 
 
• Sublimation is the transition of a substance directly from the solid to the gas state, without passing through the liquid state.
 
• Dry ice (solid carbon dioxide) sublimates at -78.5º C (-109.3º F) at standard atmospheric pressure.

questions.question: The average speed of the car on a particular stretch of road is 90 km/hr. On a particular day, the average speed was 1/5 less than on normal days, as a result, it took 16 minutes longer. What is the length (in km) of this particular stretch of road?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Normal Speed** to **Reduced Speed** = 1 : (1 − 1/5) = 5 : 4.

Since **Distance** is constant, **Time Ratio** is the inverse of **Speed Ratio** = 4 : 5.

Difference in time units = 5 − 4 = 1 unit → **16 min**.

**Normal Time** = 4 units = 4 × 16 = 64 min = 64/60 hours.

**Distance** = 90 km/hr × 64/60 hr = 96 km.

**∴ The correct answer is 96 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Normal **average speed** (S₁) = **90 km/hr**

Speed reduction = **1/5** of normal

Time increase = **16 min** = 16/60 hr = 4/15 hr

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/00396b56353886c272d41aff41a554c781de5453e8ceb60a5993c93aa56e71d5.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Reduced speed (S₂) = 90 − (1/5 × 90) = 90 − 18 = **72 km/hr**

⇒ Let the **length** of the stretch be **D** km.

⇒ Time taken at normal speed = D/90 hours

⇒ Time taken at reduced speed = D/72 hours

⇒ According to the question: D/72 − D/90 = 16/60

⇒ (5D − 4D) / 360 = 4/15

⇒ D / 360 = 4 / 15

⇒ D = (4 × 360) / 15

⇒ D = 4 × 24 = **96 km**

**∴ The correct answer is 96 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed-Time Relationship

When **distance** is constant, speed is inversely proportional to time (S ∝ 1/T). If speed becomes x/y of original, time becomes y/x of original.

Average Speed Formula

For two equal distances traveled at speeds x and y, the **Average Speed** is given by (2 × x × y) / (x + y).

Unit Conversion

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert minutes to hours, divide the value by 60.</p

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT used as an indicator to detect acid or base?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Table Salt.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Table salt** is a compound made up of **sodium and chlorine ions.**
 
• It is commonly used in food preparation and as a preservative.
 
• It is not used as an indicator to detect acid or base.
 
• It is **a neutral compound **and d**oes not show any color change when it comes in contact with an acid or a base.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• An** indicator** is a substance that changes its color when it comes in contact with an acid or a base.
 
• It helps in detecting whether a solution is acidic or basic.
 
• Two common types of indicators are :
 
 
• **pH Indicators**: examples are **Litmus paper**, **phenolphthalein**.
 
• **Redox Indicators**: examples are **Potassium permanganate.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Red cabbage** is** a natural indicator** that **changes** its color **from red to blue or green when it comes in contact with an acid or a base**.

 
 
• It is commonly used in science experiments to detect the presence of acid or base in a solution.
 
• It contains a **pigment** called **anthocyanin** that changes its color based on the pH of the solution it is in contact with.
 
 
 
• **Turmeric** is also **a natural indicator** that changes its color from yellow to red when it comes in contact with an acid or a base. .
 
 
• It is commonly used in food industry to detect the presence of acid or base in food products
 
• It is a spice commonly used in Indian and Middle Eastern cuisine.
 
• It is also known for its medicinal properties.
 
 
 
• **Litmus **is **a synthetic indicator** that **changes its color from blue to red in the presence of an acid** and **from red to blue in the presence of a base**. 
 
 
• It is one of the most commonly used indicators in chemistry experiments.
 
• It is a** mixture of dyes extracted from lichens**. 
 
• It is available in the form of strips or solution and is widely used in laboratories for detecting the pH of a solution.

questions.question: The focal length of human eye lens is (with relaxed eye)-
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** 2.5 cm**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Focal Length**: The focal length of the lens is the distance between the lens and the image sensor when the subject is in focus.
 
• The human eye encompasses a **biconvex lens**.
 
• The lens within the eye refracts the light and focuses it on the retina. 
 
• The shape of the lens changes to **regulate the focal length of the eye**, thus allowing the eye to focus clearly on objects at varying distances.
 
• The ability of the lens to adjust from far to near focus is called **accommodation.**
 
• The eye focuses on an object by bending all of the light rays from a single point on the observed object toward a single point on the retina.
 
• In the eyeball, light rays passing through the cornea are bent by its curvature toward the pupil.
 
• The lens flexes to change its curvature and finish the focusing process.
 
• When an object is located at infinity, **the focal length, or the distance from the cornea to the retina, of a normal relaxed eye is** about **2.5 cm**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Myopia: **

 
• **Myopia** is also referred to** as near-sightedness.**
 
• It** **is an eye disorder where light focuses in front of, instead of on, the retina. As a result of which, **distant objects appear blurry while close objects appear normal.**

**Hypermetropia:**

 
• Hypermetropia is also known as **far-sightedness.**
 
• **It** is the condition of the eyes where the image of a nearby object is formed behind the retina.
 
• Here, the light is focused behind the retina instead of focusing on the retina.
 
• The person suffering from hypermetropia has **difficulty seeing nearby objects clearly but can see distant objects clearly**.

**Presbyopia:**

 
• **Presbyopia is the gradual loss of your eye's ability to focus on nearby objects**. 
 
• Presbyopia usually starts in the early to mid-40s and continues to worsen until around age 65.

questions.question: What happens when pea plants showing two different characteristics (the tall/short trait and the round seed/wrinkled seed trait), rather than just one are bred with each other?

options.text: The tall/short trait and the round seed/wrinkled seed trait are independently inherited.
They are all tall and have round seeds in F2 generation.
Some F1 progeny are tall plants with round seeds, and some are short plants with wrinkled seeds.
The tall/short trait and the round seed/wrinkled seed trait are dependently inherited.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The tall/short trait and the round seed/wrinkled seed trait are independently inherited.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When pea plants showing two different characteristics are bred, each trait is inherited independently of the other.
 
• This observation is consistent with Mendel's Law of Independent Assortment, which states that alleles of different genes assort independently of one another during gamete formation.
 
• The F1 progeny will all be heterozygous, exhibiting the dominant traits for both characteristics.
 
• In the F2 generation, a 9:3:3:1 phenotypic ratio is typically observed, showing independent assortment.
 
• This means that the combination of traits can vary, resulting in plants that may be tall with round seeds, tall with wrinkled seeds, short with round seeds, or short with wrinkled seeds.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Law of Segregation**

 
 
• Mendel's first law states that the two alleles for a heritable character segregate (separate) during gamete formation and end up in different gametes.
 
• This law ensures that offspring acquire one allele from each parent for each trait.
 
 
 
• **Law of Dominance**
 
 
• According to this law, in a heterozygote, one trait will conceal the presence of another trait for the same characteristic.
 
• The dominant allele is expressed in the phenotype, while the recessive allele is masked in the presence of the dominant allele.
 
 
 
• **Monohybrid Cross**
 
 
• A cross between individuals focusing on a single trait, which illustrates the inheritance of one characteristic.
 
• It typically results in a 3:1 phenotypic ratio in the F2 generation.

questions.question: If the momentum of a body is tripled keeping the mass as constant, its Kinetic Energy will ________.

options.text: become nine times its original value
become six times its original value
become three times its original value

questions.solution:
__**CONCEPT**__:

__
 
• Kinetic energy: The **energy of an object due to its motion** is called kinetic energy.

 
 
• It is denoted by **KE**.
 
• Mathematically **kinetic energy** can be written as 
 
• Kinetic energy (KE) = 1/2 mv2
 
 
 
• **Momentum**: The **product of mass and velocity** is called **momentum **or **linear momentum**.
 
 
• It is denoted by **P**.
 
• Mathematically it can be written as 
 
• Momentum (P) = m × v
 
 
 
• The** relationship between kinetic energy and momentum** is given by:

KE=(P²)/(2m)​

Where m is mass of the object and v is the velocity

**CALCULATION**__**:**

Given - Final momentum (P₂) = 3P (initial momentum)

 
• The relationship between kinetic energy and momentum is given by:

KE=(P²)/(2m)​

 
• When the **momentum of an object is tripled keeping the mass as constant:**

**​Rightarrow {KE}₂=(P²₁)/(2m)**

Rightarrow {KE}₂=((3P)²)/(2m)=(9P²)/(2m) = 9(KE) [because KE=(P²)/(2m)]

 
• Hence, **if the momentum of a body is tripled, it's Kinetic energy will become nine times its original value**. So option 2 is correct.

questions.question: The direction of a magnetic field due to a straight current carrying conductor can be determined using:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Right hand thumb rule.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The direction of a magnetic field due to a straight current-carrying conductor can be determined using the **Right-hand thumb rule**.

 
 
• The **Right-hand thumb rule** states that if you hold the current-carrying conductor with your right hand such that the thumb points in the direction of the current, then the fingers wrapped around the conductor will point in the direction of the magnetic field lines.
 
• This rule is a practical way to determine the orientation of the magnetic field generated by electric current in a straight conductor.
 
• The magnetic field forms concentric circles around the conductor with the direction given by the right-hand thumb rule.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fleming's left-hand rule** is used to determine the direction of force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field.
 
• **Fleming's right-hand rule** is used to determine the direction of induced current when a conductor moves in a magnetic field.
 
• The **Left hand thumb rule** is not commonly used in the context of magnetic fields and current-carrying conductors.
 
• Understanding these rules is crucial for students and professionals working with electromagnetism and related fields.

questions.question: Oesophagus belongs to which major organ system in the human body?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Digestive system**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **oesophagus**, also known as the food pipe, is an integral part of the **digestive system**.
 
• Its primary function is to transport food and liquids from the **pharynx** (throat) to the **stomach** for digestion.
 
• The oesophagus is made up of layers of muscles that contract in a wave-like motion called **peristalsis** to move food downward.
 
• The oesophagus also contains the **lower esophageal sphincter (LES)**, a muscular ring that prevents stomach acid from flowing back into the oesophagus, protecting it from damage.
 
• The digestive system includes other organs like the **mouth, stomach, small intestine, large intestine, liver, and pancreas**, working together to break down food into nutrients and energy.
 
• Diseases related to the oesophagus include **acid reflux, esophagitis, and esophageal cancer**, highlighting its critical role in maintaining digestive health.
 
• The oesophagus plays no role in respiration or hormone secretion, which are functions of other organ systems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Respiratory system**__

 __
 
• The respiratory system includes organs like the **lungs, trachea, and diaphragm**.
 
• Its primary function is to facilitate the exchange of **oxygen and carbon dioxide** between the body and the environment.
 
• The oesophagus is not involved in respiration, as it is part of the digestive pathway.
 
 
 
• **Nervous system**__
 __
 
• The nervous system includes the **brain, spinal cord, and nerves**.
 
• It is responsible for transmitting signals throughout the body, controlling movements, and processing sensory information.
 
• The oesophagus is controlled by the nervous system, but it is not part of it.
 
 
 
• **Endocrine system**__
 
 
• The endocrine system is made up of glands like the **thyroid, adrenal glands, and pancreas**, which secrete hormones.
 
• These hormones regulate various bodily functions, such as metabolism, growth, and reproduction.
 
• The oesophagus does not produce or regulate hormones, so it is unrelated to the endocrine system.

questions.question: The atomic mass of an element is usually expressed in which of the following units?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Atomic mass units (amu)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Atomic mass units (amu) are the standard unit of mass that quantifies the mass of an atom or molecule.
 
• 1 amu is defined as one twelfth (1/12) of the mass of a carbon-12 atom.
 
• The atomic mass unit allows chemists to compare the masses of different atoms on a scale that is easy to use and understand.
 
• The unit is widely used in chemistry and physics to express atomic and molecular weights.
 
• Atomic mass units are essential for understanding chemical reactions, molecular structures, and isotopic compositions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Isotopes:**

 
 
• Atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons and thus different atomic masses.
 
• Examples include Carbon-12, Carbon-13, and Carbon-14.
 
 
 
• **Molar Mass:**
 
 
• The mass of one mole of a substance (usually expressed in g/mol).
 
• It is numerically equal to the atomic or molecular mass in amu but expressed in grams.
 
 
 
• **Avogadro's Number:**
 
 
• The number of atoms, ions, or molecules in one mole of a substance, approximately 6.022 x 10²³.
 
• This constant is used to convert between atomic mass units and grams.
 
 
 
• **Relative Atomic Mass:**
 
 
• A weighted average of the atomic masses of an element's isotopes.
 
• It reflects the abundance of each isotope in nature.

questions.question: Which of following compounds is used as an ingredient in antacids?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sodium hydrogen carbonate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Sodium hydrogen carbonate, also known as baking soda, is commonly used as an ingredient in antacids.
 
• It helps to neutralize stomach acid, providing relief from heartburn and indigestion.
 
• Antacids containing sodium hydrogen carbonate are effective in treating acid reflux and peptic ulcers.
 
• Sodium hydrogen carbonate reacts with hydrochloric acid in the stomach to produce carbon dioxide, water, and salt, reducing acidity.
 
• It is preferred in antacid formulations because it works quickly to relieve symptoms of hyperacidity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hydrochloric acid**

 
 
• It is a strong acid produced in the stomach to aid in digestion.
 
• Excess production of hydrochloric acid can lead to conditions like acid reflux and ulcers.
 
 
 
• **Calcium carbonate**
 
 
• It is another compound often used in antacids to neutralize stomach acid.
 
• Calcium carbonate is effective in providing longer-lasting relief compared to sodium hydrogen carbonate.
 
 
 
• **Magnesium hydroxide**
 
 
• Commonly known as milk of magnesia, it is used in antacids to neutralize stomach acid and relieve constipation.
 
• Magnesium hydroxide works by drawing water into the intestines, making it easier to pass stool.

questions.question: The brain is responsible for processing ________ (1) signals. The spinal cord transmits ________ (2) signals to the brain. The peripheral nervous system connects the brain with ________ (3).
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Electrical, sensory, muscles**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The brain processes electrical signals, which are fundamental for communication within the nervous system.
 
• The spinal cord is responsible for transmitting sensory signals to the brain, enabling the perception of touch, pain, and other sensations.
 
• The peripheral nervous system connects the brain and spinal cord to the muscles, facilitating movement and coordination.
 
• Electrical signals within neurons allow for the rapid transmission of information throughout the nervous system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Neurons:** The basic building blocks of the nervous system, neurons are specialized cells that transmit electrical and chemical signals.
 
• **Synapse:** A synapse is the junction between two neurons where electrical or chemical signals are transmitted.
 
• **Action Potential:** An action potential is a rapid rise and fall in voltage across a cellular membrane, essential for the transmission of electrical signals in neurons.
 
• **Neurotransmitters:** Chemical messengers released by neurons at synapses to relay signals to other neurons or muscles.
 
• **Reflex Arc:** A neural pathway that controls a reflex action, typically involving a sensory neuron, a motor neuron, and sometimes an interneuron, facilitating quick responses to stimuli.

questions.question: In a fluid medium, the nature of sound waves is

__Concept__:

__
 
• Sound wave: The longitudinal wave in an elastic medium that produces an audible sensation is called a sound wave.

 
 
• As sound waves are longitudinal waves, the air particles vibrate to and fro in the direction of propagation of sound.
 
• It is a wave of compression and rarefaction.

questions.question: Which body part in the human body is composed of stratified squamous epithelium?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Skin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Stratified squamous epithelium** is a type of epithelial tissue that consists of multiple layers of flat cells.
 
• The primary function of this tissue is to provide **protection** against mechanical stress, dehydration, and microbial invasion.
 
• The outermost layer of the skin, known as the **epidermis**, is composed of stratified squamous epithelium.
 
• These cells in the skin are **keratinized**, meaning they contain keratin, a protein that helps in waterproofing and providing strength.
 
• Stratified squamous epithelium is also found in other parts of the body, such as the **oesophagus and oral cavity**, but the skin's epidermis is the most prominent example.

• **Epithelial Tissue**

 
 
• Epithelial tissues are one of the four basic types of tissues in the body, along with connective tissue, muscle tissue, and nervous tissue.
 
• They cover the body surfaces, line body cavities, and form glands.
 
• Epithelial tissues are classified based on the number of layers (simple or stratified) and the shape of the cells (squamous, cuboidal, or columnar).
 
 
 
• **Keratin**
 
 
• Keratin is a type of protein found in the skin, hair, and nails.
 
• It provides structural strength and helps protect cells from damage or stress.
 
 
 
• **Oesophagus**
 
 
• The oesophagus is a muscular tube that connects the throat (pharynx) with the stomach.
 
• It is lined with non-keratinized stratified squamous epithelium, which provides protection from abrasion due to food passage.
 
 
 
• **Skin Layers**
 
 
• The skin is composed of three main layers: the epidermis, dermis, and hypodermis.
 
• The epidermis is the outermost layer, primarily made up of keratinized stratified squamous epithelium.
 
• The dermis lies beneath the epidermis and contains connective tissue, blood vessels, and nerve endings.
 
• The hypodermis, also known as the subcutaneous layer, contains fat and connective tissue that insulates and cushions the body.

• Examples of abiotic components also include sunlight, water, air, and nutrients.

• They play a crucial role in nutrient cycling within ecosystems.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Abiotic Factors**:
 
 
• Abiotic factors determine the physical environment in which biotic components live.
 
• They influence growth rates, reproductive success, and survival of organisms.
 
 
 
• **Interaction of Abiotic and Biotic Factors**:
 
 
• Both sets of components interact to create a dynamic and functional ecosystem.
 
• Changes in abiotic factors can lead to shifts in the types of biotic communities present.

questions.question: A sum becomes 27 times in 3 years, compounded annually at a certain rate of interest. Calculate annual interest rate.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For **compounded annually** growth, use the root of the times-factor based on the **time period**.

Growth factor for 3 years = 27 times.

Annual growth factor = ³√27 = 3.

Rate (R) = (Annual Factor − 1) × 100% = (3 − 1) × 100% = 200%.

**∴ The correct answer is 200%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Principal (P)** = P

**Amount (A)** = 27P

**Time (t)** = 3 years

**Formula Used:**

A = P(1 + R/100)t

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/34ee4724494690706a21abf3804daff494342e371bc0818d3a2a7a2fef55d62e.png] 

⇒ 27P = P(1 + R/100)³

⇒ 27 = (1 + R/100)³

⇒ (3)³ = (1 + R/100)³

⇒ 3 = 1 + R/100

⇒ R/100 = 3 − 1

⇒ R/100 = 2

⇒ R = 200%

**∴ The correct answer is 200%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Interest Rate

When interest is compounded more than once a year, the actual rate earned is Rₑff = [1 + (r/n)]ⁿ − 1, where 'n' is the number of compounding periods.

Difference between CI and SI

For 2 years, the difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest is CI − SI = P(R/100)².

Rule of 72

A quick shortcut to estimate the doubling time of an investment: Time ≈ 72 ÷ Rate of Interest.</p

questions.question: If Δ ABC ∼ Δ QPR, (ar(Delta ABC))/(ar(Delta PQR))=(4)/(9), AC = 12 cm, AB = 18 cm and BC = 10 cm, then PR (in cm) is equal to:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For two **similar triangles**, the ratio of their **areas** is equal to the **square** of the ratio of their corresponding sides.

Given: ΔABC ~ ΔQPR and Area(ΔABC)/Area(ΔPQR) = 4/9.

Ratio of corresponding sides = √(4/9) = 2/3.

From similarity ΔABC ~ ΔQPR, side **BC** corresponds to side **PR**.

∴ BC/PR = 2/3 ⇒ 10/PR = 2/3 ⇒ PR = (10 × 3)/2 = 15 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 15 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

ΔABC ~ ΔQPR

Area(ΔABC) / Area(ΔQPR) = 4/9

AB = 18 cm, BC = 10 cm, AC = 12 cm

**Formula Used:**

If two triangles are similar, the ratio of their areas is the square of the ratio of any two corresponding sides:

Area(Δ1) / Area(Δ2) = (Side₁ / Side₂)²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/855d7c0ee70d27a1170e359a8ffb3f4348702568ab5b4c6066018d3ad33ce671.png] 

**Calculations:**

Since ΔABC ~ ΔQPR, the corresponding sides are (AB, QP), (BC, PR), and (AC, QR).

⇒ Area(ΔABC) / Area(ΔQPR) = (BC / PR)²

⇒ 4 / 9 = (10 / PR)²

Taking square root on both sides:

⇒ √(4 / 9) = 10 / PR

⇒ 2 / 3 = 10 / PR

⇒ 2 × PR = 10 × 3

⇒ 2 × PR = 30

⇒ PR = 30 / 2

⇒ PR = 15 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 15 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area Theorem for Similar Triangles

The ratio of the areas of two similar triangles is equal to the square of the ratio of their corresponding altitudes, medians, or angle bisectors.

Perimeter of Similar Triangles

The ratio of the perimeters of two similar triangles is equal to the ratio of their corresponding sides: P1/P2 = s1/s2.

Similarity Criteria

Two triangles are similar if they satisfy the **AAA** (Angle-Angle-Angle), **SSS** (Side-Side-Side ratio), or **SAS** (Side-Angle-Side ratio) criteria.</p

questions.question: The average speed of a car is 30 km/hr without stoppage, with stoppage the average speed of the car is 20 km/hr. For how much time did the car stops in an hour?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Stoppage time per hour = (Difference in speeds ÷ Speed without stoppage) × 60 min

Difference in speeds = 30 − 20 = 10 km/hr

Stoppage time = (10 ÷ 30) × 60 = 20 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 20 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Speed (without stoppage) = 30 km/hr, Speed (with stoppage) = 20 km/hr

 
• Start (0 km) End (30 km) Ideal Path: 30 km covered in 60 min 
• 
• Actual Travel (20 km) Gap: 10 km (Lost Time) Effective Speed: 20 km/hr 

⇒ Distance covered by the car in 1 hour without stoppage = 30 km

⇒ Distance covered by the car in 1 hour with stoppage = 20 km

⇒ Decrease in distance due to stoppage = 30 − 20 = 10 km

⇒ Stoppage time = Time taken to cover the lost distance at the original speed

⇒ Time = 10 ÷ 30 hours

⇒ Time in minutes = (1 ÷ 3) × 60 = 20 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 20 min.**

Average Speed

Speed Unit Conversion

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5 ÷ 18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18 ÷ 5.

Relative Speed

If two objects move in same direction, relative speed = |S₁ − S₂|. In opposite direction, relative speed = S₁ + S₂.

questions.question: By selling 24 pens, a vendor lost the selling price of 6 pens. Find the loss percent
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the **Selling Price (SP)** of 1 pen be 1 unit.

Total **SP** of 24 pens = 24 units.

**Loss** = SP of 6 pens = 6 units.

**Cost Price (CP)** = SP + Loss = 24 + 6 = 30 units.

**Loss %** = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100 = (6 ÷ 30) × 100 = 20%.

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Number of pens sold = 24, Loss = SP of 6 pens.

**Formulas:** Loss = CP − SP | Loss% = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a5b569e6bd68cc90cbc940e036bdc0326cfdc01fa0d26fb961e038eff1be2c93.png] 

⇒ Let SP of 1 pen = x.

⇒ SP of 24 pens = 24x.

⇒ Loss = 6x.

⇒ CP of 24 pens = SP + Loss = 24x + 6x = 30x.

⇒ Loss% = (6x ÷ 30x) × 100.

⇒ Loss% = (1 ÷ 5) × 100 = 20%.

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

Concept of Loss in terms of SP

When loss is expressed in terms of **Selling Price**, the **Cost Price** is always higher than the total units sold. Formula: CP = Units Sold + Loss Units.

Concept of Profit in terms of SP

When profit is expressed in terms of **Selling Price**, the **Cost Price** is lower than the total units sold. Formula: CP = Units Sold − Profit Units.</p

questions.question: Find the greatest number 23a68b, which is divisible by 3 but NOT divisible by 9.

**Given:** A number in the form **23a68b** that is divisible by **3** but **not** divisible by **9**.

**Formula Used:** Sum of digits rule for divisibility.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/04a4ccb9b657a8476ab0f84e3086f7260bfe1ab291b3d175335200c0d896317d.png] 

Checking each option systematically:

⇒ For **239685**: Sum = 2 + 3 + 9 + 6 + 8 + 5 = **33**. Since 33 ÷ 3 = 11 and 33 is not divisible by 9. (Valid)

⇒ For **239688**: Sum = 2 + 3 + 9 + 6 + 8 + 8 = **36**. Since 36 ÷ 9 = 4, it is divisible by 9. (Invalid)

⇒ For **237687**: Sum = 2 + 3 + 7 + 6 + 8 + 7 = **33**. Since 33 ÷ 3 = 11 and 33 is not divisible by 9. (Valid)

⇒ Comparing valid options 239685 and 237687, we find that **239685** is the greatest.

**∴ The correct answer is 239685.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility by 3

A number is divisible by 3 if the **sum of its digits** is a multiple of 3.

Divisibility by 9

A number is divisible by 9 if the **sum of its digits** is a multiple of 9. Note that all numbers divisible by 9 are also divisible by 3.

Relationship between 3 and 9

To be divisible by 3 but **NOT** by 9, the sum of the digits must be in the set {3, 6, 12, 15, 21, 24, 30, 33, 39, ...} excluding multiples of 9.</p

questions.question: If the square of maximum area is to be taken out from a circular steel plate of radius 28 cm, then find the area of remaining part of the circular steel plate. (cm²)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Side of **maximum square** in circle = **√2 × radius**

Area of **Remaining part** = Area of **Circle** − Area of **Square**

Area = (π × r²) − (2 × r²) = r²(π − 2)

Calculation → 28² × (22/7 − 2) = 784 × (8/7) = 112 × 8 = 896 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 896 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of the **circular plate** (r) = 28 cm

**Formula Used:**

Area of **Circle** = πr²

For a square of maximum area inside a circle, the **diagonal** of the square = **diameter** of the circle.

Area of **Square** = (Diagonal²) ÷ 2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a422388e6e4b0bbcdc4bf1f8a5e9cecd5dc38a26858a2a1be603824647a10893.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area of **Circle** = (22/7) × 28 × 28

⇒ Area of **Circle** = 22 × 4 × 28 = 2464 cm²

⇒ **Diagonal** of square = 2 × radius = 2 × 28 = 56 cm

⇒ Area of **Square** = (56 × 56) ÷ 2 = 3136 ÷ 2 = 1568 cm²

⇒ **Remaining part** = 2464 − 1568

⇒ **Remaining part** = 896 cm²

questions.question: What is the value of, sin 150° × cos 0° × tan 67° × tan 23° × tan 45°
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

If the sum of two angles A and B is 90°, then tan A × tan B = 1.

Here, 67° + 23° = 90° ⇒ tan 67° × tan 23° = 1

Also we know the standard values: sin 150° = 1 / 2, cos 0° = 1, and tan 45° = 1.

Result = (1 / 2) × 1 × 1 × 1 = 1 / 2

**∴ The correct answer is 1 / 2.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression = sin 150° × cos 0° × tan 67° × tan 23° × tan 45°

**Formula Used:**

⇒ sin(180° − θ) = sin θ

⇒ tan(90° − θ) = cot θ

⇒ tan θ × cot θ = 1

**Calculation:**

⇒ sin 150° = sin(180° − 30°) = sin 30° = 1 / 2

⇒ cos 0° = 1

⇒ tan 67° = tan(90° − 23°) = cot 23°

⇒ tan 67° × tan 23° = cot 23° × tan 23° = 1

⇒ tan 45° = 1

Substituting all the simplified values back into the expression:

⇒ Expression = (1 / 2) × 1 × 1 × 1

⇒ Expression = 1 / 2

**∴ The correct answer is 1 / 2.**

**__Additional Information__**

Complementary Angles in Trigonometry

Two angles are complementary if their sum is 90°. Key transformations: tan(90° − θ) = cot θ | sin(90° − θ) = cos θ | sec(90° − θ) = cosec θ.

Supplementary Angles

Two angles are supplementary if their sum is 180°. In the second quadrant, sine is positive: sin(180° − θ) = sin θ. Cosine and tangent are negative: cos(180° − θ) = −cos θ | tan(180° − θ) = −tan θ.

Important Trigonometric Product Rule

Whenever the sum of two angles A and B is 90° (A + B = 90°), the product of their tangents is always 1: tan A × tan B = 1.

questions.question: What is the median of the distribution: 34, 22, 13, 11, 27, 19, 25, 16?

The middle terms are the 4th and 5th terms, which are 19 and 22.

**__Alternate Method__**

**Formula:** Median = [(n/2)th term + (n/2 + 1)th term] ÷ 2 (when n is even)

⇒ Median = 41 ÷ 2 = 20.5

Median for Odd Number of Terms

If the total number of observations (n) is odd, the **Median** is the ((n + 1) ÷ 2)th term after arranging the data in order.

Empirical Relationship

For a moderately skewed distribution, the relationship between **Mean**, **Median**, and **Mode** is: Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean.

Mean (Average)

The **Mean** is calculated by dividing the sum of all observations by the total number of observations.</p

Upstream Speed

Downstream Speed

questions.question: The roots of the equation 9(x + 9)² = 441 are :
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Divide 441 by 9 directly to get **49**.

Taking the **square root** of both sides: x + 9 = ±7.

Calculate the two values: x = −9 + 7 and x = −9 − 7.

The resulting roots are **−2** and **−16**.

**∴ The correct answer is −2, −16.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given Equation:** 9(x + 9)² = 441

**Method:** Solve the **quadratic equation** by isolating the squared term and taking square roots.

⇒ 9(x + 9)² = 441

⇒ (x + 9)² = 441 ÷ 9

⇒ (x + 9)² = 49

⇒ x + 9 = √49 or x + 9 = −√49

⇒ x + 9 = 7 or x + 9 = −7

⇒ x = 7 − 9 or x = −7 − 9

⇒ x = −2 or x = −16

**∴ The correct answer is −2, −16.**

**__Additional Information__**

Square Root Property

If u² = d, then u = ±√d. This property is used to solve equations of the form (x − h)² = k by taking the root of both sides.

Quadratic Formula

For any equation ax² + bx + c = 0, the roots can be found using x = [−b ± √(b² − 4ac)] ÷ 2a.

Nature of Roots

The discriminant D = b² − 4ac determines the nature. If D > 0 and a perfect square, roots are **real, rational, and unequal**.</p

questions.question: A cricketer was averaging 49 runs after 9 innings. How many runs does she need to score in her 10th innings the take the average to 52?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Increase in **average** = 52 − 49 = 3 runs.

Total increase needed for 9 previous **innings** = 9 × 3 = 27.

Runs required in **10th innings** = New Average + Total increase = 52 + 27 = 79.

**∴ The correct answer is 79.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d9b6e2bf6f664b7bbca56b5381ab932e32ffd1d61099d8608c913eef9a9a633e.png] 

**Given:**

Initial **average** (9 innings) = 49 runs

Required **average** (10 innings) = 52 runs

**Formula Used:**

Total runs = Average × Number of innings

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total runs after **9 innings** = 9 × 49 = 441

⇒ Total runs after **10 innings** = 10 × 52 = 520

⇒ Runs needed in **10th innings** = Total runs (10 innings) − Total runs (9 innings)

⇒ Runs needed = 520 − 441 = 79

**∴ The correct answer is 79.**

**__Additional Information__**

Arithmetic Average

The average of a set of observations is the sum of the observations divided by the number of observations (Average = Sum ÷ n).

Change in Average

When a new value is added to a group, the new value = New Average + [Previous Count × (New Average − Old Average)].

Weighted Average

The combined average of two groups is given by (n₁x₁ + n₂x₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).</p

• **Padma Shri** is the fourth-highest civilian award in India after Bharat Ratna, Padma Vibhushan, and Padma Bhushan.

• In the year **2026**, a total of **8 persons** were awarded the Padma Shri in the Sports Category.

• **Padma Awards:**

 
 
• Established in **1954**, these awards are given in various disciplines like art, social work, public affairs, science and engineering, trade and industry, medicine, literature and education, sports, and civil service.
 
• They are conferred by the **President of India** at a ceremonial event held at Rashtrapati Bhavan.
 
 
 
• **Selection Process:**
 
 
• Nominations for Padma awards are invited from the general public and are also recommended by state governments, Union territories, ministries, and institutions.

questions.question: Which insurance company launched ‘Eco Assure’, a specialized add-on cover offering for commercial vehicles?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bajaj General Insurance.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **Bajaj General Insurance Limited has introduced ‘Eco Assure’, an innovative add-on cover specifically designed for commercial vehicle owners.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Depreciation Waiver:** The policy provides a **100% waiver** on depreciation if reconditioned parts are used and a **25% waiver** for new parts.
 
• **Financial Relief:** It eliminates the **Compulsory Deductible** during claims, reducing the immediate out-of-pocket expenses for vehicle operators.
 
• **Plan Variants:** It offers two versions: **Eco Assure Essential** (basic repairs, towing) and **Eco Assure Advantage** (legal costs, electric/hybrid system cover).
 
• **Coverage:** Includes 100% protection for paintwork and external body parts like bumpers, bonnets, and lamps.

__
 
• Add-on Cover__

 __
 
• An add-on is an extra protection layer that can be purchased over a standard comprehensive insurance policy to cover specific risks not included in the base plan.
 
 
 
• Compulsory Deductible__
 
 
• This is the fixed amount a policyholder must pay before the insurance company covers the rest of the claim. Eco Assure helps waive this for commercial operators.

questions.question: Disadvantage of deforestation is
questions.solution:
__Concept:__

__
 
• Deforestation is the permanent removal of trees to make room for something besides the forest.
 
• This can include clearing the land for agriculture or grazing or using the timber for fuel, construction, or manufacturing. 

Explanation:__

**Increase in soil erosion:**

__
 
• Deforestation is one of the major causes of soil erosion.
 
• Plants keep soils bound in locks of roots, and thus, prevent erosion.
 
• They also add humus to the soil by shedding leaves and twigs.
 
• Forests have been denuded practically in most parts of India but their effect on soil erosion is more in hilly parts of the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

**Consequences of deforestation:**

__
 
• Reduction in groundwater.
 
• Exposing soil to heat and rain
 
• Flooding
 
• Loss of biodiversity
 
• Displacement of indigenous communities
 
• Climate change
 
• Economic loss
 
• Landslides
 
• Decreased rainfall

**Thus, the disadvantage of deforestation is Increase in soil erosion.**__

questions.question: With reference to Rare Earth Elements (REEs), which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: Rare earth elements are geologically scarce minerals found only in a few countries, which explains China’s dominance in their global supply.
China’s dominance in rare earth supply chains is largely due to its extensive refining and processing capacity rather than exclusive control over mineral reserves.
All rare earth elements are radioactive in nature and therefore unsuitable for large-scale commercial applications.
Rare earth elements are primarily used in conventional thermal power generation and have limited relevance for clean energy technologies.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2 **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• India has announced the creation of rare earth corridors to reduce dependence on Chinese imports by strengthening domestic mining, processing, and manufacturing capabilities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• Rare earth elements are not particularly rare in terms of geological occurrence; deposits exist in several countries including India, Australia, and Brazil. **Hence, Option A is incorrect**.
 
• China dominates the rare earth supply chain mainly due to its long-standing strength in refining, processing, and downstream manufacturing rather than sheer resource availability. **Hence, Option B is correct**.
 
• Only a few rare earths like promethium are radioactive; most REEs are widely used in commercial and industrial applications. **Hence, Option C is incorrect**.
 
• Rare earth elements are critical for clean energy technologies such as electric vehicles, wind turbines, electronics, and defence systems. **Hence, Option D is incorrect**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Rare earth elements consist of 17 metals, including the lanthanide series along with scandium and yttrium.
 
• Control over processing and refining stages often determines strategic dominance in critical mineral supply chains.
 
• China accounts for a disproportionately high share of global rare earth refining capacity, giving it leverage despite the availability of deposits elsewhere.
 
• India’s rare earth potential is largely associated with monazite-bearing beach sands, but downstream processing capacity remains limited.
